name: Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd
title: Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd - 544603 - Earning Call Transcript

read.thesis: Discount-broker/platform call with no supply-side content; growth driven by MTF (book adds ~INR600-700 crores a quarter at 14.95% yield) and cash yields up ~5% YoY, but management gave no numbers on new products, Fisdom, or wealth and was evasive on the data questions.

triggers.quote: cash yields has improved by roughly 5% and we expect that to kind of keep increasing every quarter

triggers.label: MTF book adds INR600-700 cr a quarter
triggers.quote: we are seeing that roughly INR600 crores to INR700 crores getting added on a quarterly basis on the book side

triggers.label: Derivatives softness; F&O dip tied to volatility
triggers.quote: I think it was more correlated with again war than anything else

guidance.value: Slight inflationary increase over coming quarters
guidance.quote: We expect this cost to continue as is with slight inflationary increase over coming quarters.

red_flags.quote: Numbers it's bit kind of it will not make sense, like basically numbers will not give you the right data.

red_flags.label: Stagnant MAU/DAU; MTF active users flat
red_flags.quote: those numbers look fairly stagnant. In fact, DAUs have come off slightly from what it was in 4Q

evasions.quote: I think this quarter is bit too early to kind of comment about them

evasions.quote: we don't kind of disclose those kind of numbers, that's like too much detail

summary.headline: Groww Q1 FY27 call: management gave few hard numbers; MTF yield fixed at 14.95%, cash yields up ~5% YoY, and F&O softness attributed to volatility, not SEBI rules.
summary.overview: Management, led by co-founders Lalit Keshre (CEO) and Ishan Bansal (CFO), framed the quarter around building a wealth management platform and launching multiple products. Credit (LAS) now makes up 34% of disbursements, bonds launched last quarter are scaling, and SEBI and CCI approvals were received for the State Street Global partnership in the AMC. Management attributed F&O and order softness to volatility and to gold/silver ETF slowdown rather than regulation, and said Q4 FY26 was an anomaly for MTF and derivatives. Several data requests were declined or deferred, including CAC detail, revenue split, Fisdom/AMC revenue, and new-customer ARPU.

financial_highlights.change: ~+5% YoY; mgmt expects +1-2 pp per quarter as MTF penetration rises

financial_highlights.metric: Customer acquisition cost (CAC) per new NTU
financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR1,400 in Q4 FY26 per analyst; ~INR1,000 in Q4 per another reference (analyst-stated)

financial_highlights.value: ~INR23,000 crore (as recalled by management, 'INR2 3,000 or something')
~0.13 million (analyst-stated, flat across the two periods)

segments.name: Lending (MTF / LAS)
segments.commentary: MTF growth ahead of plan partly on markets; ticket size rising, but early Q2 MTF book flattish per analyst, which management tied to end-of-quarter market moves. LAS is 34% of disbursements.

segments.name: Broking (cash and F&O)
segments.commentary: Management says F&O dip in June-July tracked volatility (Iran war news), not SEBI rules. Cash order decline is mainly ETF (gold/silver) slowdown, per management. Derivatives are stabilising vs Q3.

segments.name: Commodities
segments.commentary: More than 28% retail share of notional ADTO; described as at an advanced adoption stage.

segments.name: AMC / Fisdom / Wealth
segments.commentary: SEBI and CCI approvals received for the State Street Global partnership in the AMC. Fisdom revenue has not yet shown significant improvement; W and Prime traction too early to quantify.

guidance_outlook: Cash yields expected to keep rising near term, by roughly 1-2 pp per quarter, as MTF penetration grows; no ceiling given.
Cost to operate expected to stay flat-to-slightly-up with inflationary increases; Q1 showed a slight improvement vs Q4 which had one-time risk costs.
Employee cost rise this quarter attributed to April appraisal cycle, not headcount; long-run headcount not expected to rise significantly.
US stocks via GIFT City license: testing underway, launch 'soon' but no firm date; to start with US stocks only.
Management declined to give AUM or size targets for wealth or three-to-four-year product roadmap; pipeline described as strong for next 1-2 years.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Products at different life stages: commodities advanced; US stocks just starting; W still being refined.
Multi-pod org structure used to launch new products from existing teams, per management.
MTF infrastructure issues being fixed internally, which management says will lift penetration and ticket size.
demand_pricing: Analyst view: MTF active users flat at ~0.13 million while the book grew sharply; DAU came off slightly from Q4.
Management said Q4 FY26 was an anomaly for MTF and derivatives because markets fell into quarter-end; Q1 ended positive.
Interest income rose on higher yields, not balances; float income up QoQ despite lower volumes vs Q4.
Management said the 2% ELM margin change (Nov 2024) cannot be isolated because five changes happened together. It declined to comment on reported expiry-day margin news.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost rise a sign of hiring for a wealth transition, and what is the 2-3 year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said the rise is mainly the April appraisal cycle, not headcount. Headcount is not expected to rise significantly, with wealth to be AI- and tech-led alongside RMs. ESOPs are about 10% of employee cost in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is MTF yield accretive for the cash business, and how far can acceptance go?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash yields are up ~5% YoY and are expected to rise 1-2 pp per quarter as MTF penetration grows. Adoption is still early, and ticket size can expand as infra issues are resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did active derivatives customers soften sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said Q4 FY26 was an exception with war-driven volatility that started in Q4. Compared with Q3, the trend is improving and stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and scope of US stock options via GIFT City, and effect of F&O margin changes?
qa_highlights.answer: US stocks licensed and in testing, launch 'soon' with no exact date; start with US stocks. On the expiry margin news, management said it cannot comment on news, and the Nov 2024 change cannot be isolated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the July F&O dip due to SEBI rules, and is the cash order decline 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the F&O dip to volatility (Iran war news), with regulation impact smaller than the industry expected and not material for Groww. The cash order decline reflects slowing ETF (gold/silver) activity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CAC rise sharply, and what is the affluent customer retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said the rise reflects about two months of IPL spend versus one week in Q4, with brand benefit and weaker acquisition. Affluent retention is near 100% because AUM stickiness is high.

risks_watch: Volatility-driven F&O and cash volumes; early Q2 MTF book flattish per analyst.
CAC step-up from IPL spend; management says it will normalise, but no figure was given.
Possible F&O expiry-day margin changes (management could not confirm reports).
Fisdom and AMC still in gestation, with revenue under 2% of total.
Product sprawl (US stocks, W, Prime, bonds, commodities) executed by the existing team; no financial targets given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the product pipeline and long-run wealth ambition, but evasive on numbers: management declined to quantify W, Prime, US stocks, ARPU, revenue split, and CAC detail, citing being 'too early'. Explanations for the F&O and MTF softness were framed as market-driven and largely defensive.
key_quotes: So I think on both all these three products, be it US stocks, Prime and W, I think this quarter is bit too early to kind of comment about them, but maybe in coming quarters we'll talk more about them.
So, our expectation is that in the near term it'll definitely go up, but difficult to kind of estimate where will it stop.

So, cash yields are improving. So, we've been seeing that on a year-on-year basis I think cash yields has improved by roughly 5% and we expect that to kind of keep increasing every quarter a percentage or two as the penetration of MTF keep on increasing.

growth.why: No hard revenue or EBITDA growth guidance; management guided only to cash yields rising ~1-2 pp per quarter from MTF penetration and a flat-to-slightly-up cost base, with product launches (US stocks via GIFT City, W, wealth) lacking firm dates or numbers, and declined AUM or size targets.
